items.title: Danny Barker Interview, 1976-02-04
items.q: Papa Celestine had two, at one time

ctx.x: some people have indicated that he really wanted Louis to stay with him in Chicago when Louis left and went to New York, and that I think Lil Armstrong, his wife, his second wife, sort of had an influence on his leaving the band. Do you think there was any bitterness on Joe's part when Louis left to go to Chicago?

Oh, that's not no bitterness. I don't think there was no, there was no bitterness, but it was a sort of a, a loss to Joe because there was a tradition in New Orleans to have two trumpets in the band. Papa Celestine had two, at one time, Manny Perez had two, first and second trumpet. And, uh, other bands around had two trumpets, and you played second. And it was guys, it's just like baseball, a second string catcher, you dig, more than one pitcher, and, uh, or more than one quarterback in a, a football team. It…

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: That’s one and the same. The Savoy and the Lincoln. I played there when we went to Chicago on the excursion. We played there. I told you David Jones just waved at Louis. Never come and hugged like two long lost brothers. And Louis always held that in to him, I guess. Their old grudges. Last time I seen David Jones, I working at Lee Collins’s band. Never made no money with that band. All we did was flop. Nobody came out, because Lee Collins had competition there. Papa Celestin was out there. Chris Kelly was out…
Let me ask you this. When you . . . after you . . . you went to Chicago first in 1921. When was the next time you went?

items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: And Papa Celestin, he was there playing his beautiful sweet trumpet

ctx.x: Yeah, she played piano. And they were sweethearts, and they eventually married. And Papa Celestin, he was there playing his beautiful sweet trumpet, you know, playing with the mute. He wasn't a hot... He played beautiful sweet trumpet. He played like first trumpet. He played beautiful melodies. And a reed section. Now, I had been hearing these Jazz bands with one clarinet. All of a sudden, I hear this full-sounding orchestra. Goddamn, they sounded good. Simon Marrero on bass, man. And they're playing. And that…

And Guy Kelly had started playing Louis Armstrong's thing. 'Everybody Loves Ma Baby' -- he played that on the trumpet. And he played 'What Did I Do To Be So Black and Blue?' [SINGS REFRAIN] And he was playing, and just like it was so easy... And he had a straw hat, and it was pulled down all around him. And he was an outstanding figure. He played so masterfully. See, these other guys, they played with the trumpet on the side of their lip or they looked like they were searching for something. Not Guy.

Well, the D is blind and she's sick. Her mind is gone. She was in neurology at the Charity Hospital. All the doctors said what a brilliant woman she was. You know, to still retain everything she could. Now here, where is that? That was taken at the Tulane Club, I guess. John Casimir. Who are the other guys?
Oh, Fernandez, Albert Walters. And Anderson. Oh yeah, I can see now who that guy is. Paul Ballman.
